Branches snagged at her sleeves, pulling her back like hesitant fingers, but she pressed on, each footfall a muffled thump against the carpet of fallen leaves. Light filtered through the canopy above, dappling her path in patches of gold, but shadows lurked in the corners of her vision, whispering secrets she wasn’t sure she wanted to hear.

“Lila!” The voice cut through the stillness like a knife, sharp and urgent. It was Ethan, his tone a mixture of worry and irritation. She turned, brushing a strand of hair from her forehead, her heart pounding not just from the exertion but from something deeper—a knot of anxiety that twisted tighter with every glance back toward him.

“Why are you yelling?” she shot back, trying to mask the tremor in her voice. The last thing she needed was for him to see her fear. She didn’t want to admit how alone she felt out here, even with him trailing close behind.

“Because you’re running off again! Just wait up, will you?” He stepped into the clearing, his face flushed, hands on his hips. The sunlight caught the worry etched in his features, the way his brow furrowed like storm clouds gathering on the horizon.

Every moment they spent in these woods felt like a fleeting chance to escape the mundane, to chase something wild and untamed.

The forest around them seemed to close in, the rustle of leaves and distant calls of unseen creatures amplifying the tension. Lila felt the cool brush of the breeze against her skin, a reminder of how alive everything was in this moment, how vibrant the world felt beyond the confines of their everyday lives. Yet, Ethan’s worry wrapped around her like a too-tight cloak, stifling her excitement.

She shifted her weight from one foot to the other, her fingers tugging at the hem of her shirt. “I’m fine,” she insisted, though her voice quivered, betraying the unease gnawing at her insides. “I just wanted to see what was ahead.”

Ethan’s gaze softened, the tightness in his jaw easing as he took a breath, his shoulders dropping slightly. “I get that. But we’re in the middle of nowhere. Just…let’s stick together, okay?” He stepped closer, his hand reaching out to rest on her shoulder, grounding her in the moment. His touch was warm, a steady reminder that she wasn’t truly alone, even if her heart raced with the thrill of the unknown.
